title: Vesper and the Contact
premise: Cyrus Kavanagh, a ghost investigator for a financial-crimes unit that launders its own findings, is handed the impossible: Flight 4471 never landed, yet every passenger disembarked, and the paper trail has been erased mid-flight. Following the money, he discovers the 'Contact' — an inheritance broker who launders not cash but identities, trained by the very network Cyrus's own agency grew from. To burn it down he must ally with Vesper, the Contact's estranged daughter and his only witness, choosing loyalty to a found family over the institution that made him. In the end Cyrus torches the network's ledger at the cost of his career and name, while Vesper inherits what remains — and chooses to end the trade rather than run it.
about_author: Marguerite Halloran is a former compliance auditor who spent a decade tracing shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose ledgers and loyalties refuse to balance.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He closes another case no one will ever credit, scrubbing a senator's cousin clean for his own agency. The emotional beat is quiet corrosion: he's good at making truth disappear, and it's starting to feel like complicity.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A routine flag: an aircraft still airborne whose passenger manifest, booking records, and radar history vanish in real time. He watches the erasure happen live. Beat: cold fascination curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She was on 4471 and got off before takeoff; her father's people erased everyone else. She recognizes the signature of the wipe because she was raised inside it. Beat: fear sharpened into intent.

chapters.title: Attribution Denied
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. His director orders the file sealed and Cyrus assigned elsewhere — then quietly reassigns him to find whoever leaked it. He realizes he's being used as both broom and blade. Beat: betrayal.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Cyrus traces a survivor claim to Vesper; she's expecting him and has already copied his credentials. They strike an uneasy bargain over bad coffee. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback woven through present: her father Aurel, the Contact, taught her that identity is the only currency that appreciates. She reveals 4471 carried eleven new lives, not passengers. Beat: grief braided with resentment.

chapters.title: The Training Floor
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following funding trails, he finds the academy where the network trains its launderers — and recognizes instructors seconded from his own agency years ago. Beat: vertigo; the rot runs upstream.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She leads Cyrus to a dead drop her father still uses, retrieving a partial client list. A watcher follows them home. Beat: intimacy built on shared danger.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The list yields eleven assumed identities, one of which belongs to a sitting regulator — the man who ordered the file sealed. Beat: the conspiracy has a face, and it signs his paychecks.

chapters.title: What Fathers Keep
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She confronts Aurel at a gallery opening; he offers her the succession instead of answers. She takes the offer to her teeth and lies. Beat: love weaponized.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The agency brands him compromised; his access dies account by account while he watches. Someone inside is protecting him from worse. Beat: exile, and a flicker of unexpected mercy.

chapters.title: The Quiet Partner
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They identify the internal protector: a retired handler who helped train Aurel and now wants the network buried before pension season. Beat: cynical alliance, first real hope.

chapters.title: Ledger of Selves
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The master ledger — every manufactured identity since 1989 — sits in a vault under Aurel's vineyard. She knows the locks because she grew up picking them. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The regulator schedules a 'records integrity audit' — a cover for destroying the vault remotely. Seventy-two hours. Beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: Vineyard Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Reconnaissance of the estate; Vesper walks Cyrus through her childhood geography, every camera and dog and blind spot a memory. Beat: tenderness under tactical language.

chapters.title: The Regulator's Confession
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He corners the regulator with recorded evidence; the man confesses to buying his own second life and offers Cyrus a cut. Cyrus declines on tape. Beat: moral line drawn in ink.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Aurel learns of her betrayal — not through surveillance but through her own tell, a habit he taught her. He lets her come anyway. Beat: heartbreak disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Inside the vault, Aurel waits. He offers Cyrus the thing he's always wanted: attribution, credit, a name. Cyrus hesitates one beat too long — long enough for the remote purge to begin. Beat: temptation, then sirens.

chapters.title: Firewall
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Climax part one: Cyrus physically severs the vault's uplink while Vesper fights her father among the server racks. The handler sacrifices himself holding the door. Beat: desperate, kinetic, costly.

chapters.title: Ash Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Climax part two: she chooses which copy survives — none intact. Aurel, wounded, watches his life's work burn and finally tells her the truth about her mother's erased identity. Beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Fallout: the scandal breaks without a hero; Cyrus declines reinstatement and hands the recordings to a journalist anonymously. For once, the work speaks without his name on it. Beat: release.

chapters.title: What Vesper Kept
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, coda. Months later, she and Cyrus run a small firm recovering stolen identities for their rightful owners. Her father's last gift — one genuine record, her mother's — sits framed on the wall. Beat: found family, chosen inheritance.
